verdict.line: You lose if Kled lands repeated Q hooks and Jousting poke before you ever reach 50+ Fury; you win once you've ground Skaarl's health down and he dismounts into a weaker, un-hooked state.

brief.thesis: Kled mounted on Skaarl has a longer effective threat range than Renekton everywhere in his kit — an 800-range Q hook and a 550-range Jousting dash against Renekton's 325/300/450-range tools — so early trades favor Kled and explain his measured solo-kill edge. Renekton's counter is structural rather than positional: every point of Fury past 50 upgrades Cull the Meek's damage and heal and turns Ruthless Predator into a 3-hit, shield-destroying, 1.5-second stun, so the fight inverts once you can stack Fury and grind Skaarl's bar down to force a dismount, after which Kled deals less damage to champions outright.

theirWindow.when: Kled's Q off cooldown, you're in range
theirWindow.what: Bear Trap on a Rope (Q, 800 range, 11/10/9/8/7s cooldown) can hook and yank you in from well outside your kit before he follows with Jousting (E) and the four-attack speed burst of Violent Tendencies (W); don't stand where that hook lands clean.

yourWindow.when: Fury above 50 and Kled still mounted
yourWindow.what: Commit now: Cull the Meek (Q) hits harder and heals more, and Ruthless Predator (W) becomes a 3-hit sequence that strips shields and stuns for 1.5 seconds — long enough to land your full combo and chunk Skaarl's health toward a dismount.

powerCurve.note: Q hook outranges your whole kit
R adds HP and Fury generation

start.why: Kled's Q hook and early all-ins are built to chip health before you can swing back; the extra base HP and regen smooths through that poke, and it's the measured 66.7% win rate start in this matchup (21 games) versus Doran's Blade's 41.4%.

boots.why: Dulls the four-attack burst from Violent Tendencies (W) and general auto-trades, which is the main way Kled punishes you before you reach Fury breakpoints.

core.why: Its shield-break effect lines up with your own W (Ruthless Predator) shredding shields at 50+ Fury, guaranteeing real damage through any defensive tech during the all-in.
The armor shred stacks with Slice and Dice's (E) empowered armor reduction, so your autos and W chunk Skaarl's bar down faster toward the dismount.
Highest-sample completed path (33.3% win rate, 29.4% pick); the bleed-and-heal-back sustain offsets Kled's ranged poke over the repeated short trades this lane requires.

situational.when: kled's poke is outpacing your sustain and you need raw survivability to keep forcing fights
you're already ahead and want to shorten W's cooldown to chain stuns across skirmishes
kled keeps disengaging mounted or you need to run down a dismounted, fleeing target

runes.keystoneWhy: The stacking adaptive force and healing reward the long, repeated trades this matchup demands — Skaarl doesn't go down in one exchange, and Conqueror's sustain keeps you winning the war of attrition toward the dismount.

summoners.why: This is the measured best-performing combo here (50% win rate, 13.5% pick) and fits the matchup's defensive shape: freeze under tower through Kled's hook poke, then teleport back in once Eclipse and Black Cleaver are online.

playing.title: Respect the 800-range hook
playing.detail: Kled's Q (Bear Trap on a Rope) outranges every tool you have; don't trade at a distance where he can land it clean, especially while both his Q and E are up.

playing.title: Farm Fury before committing
playing.detail: Push Fury past 50 on minions or safe pokes before you engage — under 50, Cull the Meek and Ruthless Predator are both at their weak breakpoint and you're trading at a mechanical disadvantage.

playing.title: All-in only with the 1.5s W stun ready
playing.detail: Only commit your full combo when Ruthless Predator (W) is empowered; its 1.5-second, shield-destroying 3-hit stun is long enough to land Q and E behind it, while the base 0.75-second stun just gives Kled time to Jousting away.

playing.title: Track Skaarl's bar, not Kled's
playing.detail: Kled deals less damage to champions once dismounted and loses the Q hook for the far weaker Pocket Pistol — sustained damage onto Skaarl's health, not Kled's own HP, is what actually disarms him.

playing.title: Don't walk into the return Jousting pass
playing.detail: Kled's E (Jousting) can be recast to dash back through his original target for a second hit of the same damage; stepping forward after the first dash eats that return pass for free.

playing.title: Save E to close, not to poke
playing.detail: Slice and Dice (450 range) is your only tool that matches Kled's reach — hold it to close distance after he commits Q or E rather than burning your one gap-closer early on its 16-to-10s cooldown.

playing.title: Grind for the dismount, not first blood
playing.detail: Kled holds the measured solo-kill advantage here, so don't force all-ins to win exchanges outright; chip Skaarl's health down over repeated short trades and only go all-in once he's dismounted or your Fury and W stun are both ready.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and the Renekton vs. Kled win-rate figures above come from measured games on the current patch (16.20.1) via OP.GG; the Fury-threshold and forced-dismount timing read is my own tactical judgment, not a measured stat.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of being hit with Kled’s (Q). Engage aggressively repeatedly after building up Fury to force Kled to dismount Skaarl.
